Sasha P.: quick follow-up to the on‑prem packaging RFC — been thinking about a different tradeoff: instead of monolithic seed+delta bundles, what about a "sideloaded OCI-layer" approach for airgapped installs?

Sasha P.: idea in one line: produce content‑addressed OCI layers (tarballs signed and notarized) plus a small indexed manifest that lists layer refs and apply graph. Operator can provide a USB or HTTP bundle containing the subset of layers they have; the installer applies and fetches missing layers from a controlled mirror when available.

Maria L.: hmm. that could reduce duplicate payloads across versions, since layers dedupe. also makes airgap delivery align with existing OCI tooling, which ops already know. :+1:

Kevin T.: what about verification and atomic activation? we need to avoid partially applied states if a layer is missing mid-apply.

Sasha P.: good point. plan is: 1) two-phase apply — stage (verify signatures + unpack to staging area) then activate (switch symlink/rename). 2) manifest includes a transactional activation marker and precomputed hash chain so verifier can prove completeness before handoff.

Jun (infra): storage-constrained devices worry me. Some customers only allow a single spare disk. Staging + full layers could blow past free space.

Sasha P.: agreed. to address that: allow a streaming-apply mode where the install pipeline supports delta-patching layered files in-place (apply binary deltas inside layers) and a "sparse fetch" mode where only file-refs needed by minimal boot are included, rest fetched later. The manifest would declare optional vs required layers.

Maria L.: can you sketch what the manifest looks like? short pseudo example would help ops teams review.

Sasha P.: sure — minimal example (pseudo):
```
manifest: {
  version: "v1",
  bundles: [
    {ref: "sha256:aaa...", size: 1.2GB, required: true, signature: "sig1"},
    {ref: "sha256:bbb...", size: 120MB, required: false, signature: "sig2", optional_after: "activate"}
  ],
  activation: {marker_path: "/opt/rw/active_v", hash_chain_root: "sha256:ccc..."}
}
```

Jun (infra): nice. how does this interplay with our existing verifier agent and seed handshake?

Sasha P.: verifier agent unchanged for core crypto checks — we add a small "layer-index" endpoint to the handshake so operator can say "I have these layer refs" and the control plane can instruct which layers to include in the USB bundle. The offline operator tooling would produce a locator file that maps layer refs -> file names.

Kevin T.: rollout semantics? patch vs full upgrade?

Sasha P.: manifest supports a graph with edges to express replacement/patch rules. For rollouts: the control plane can generate incremental manifests that list only changed layers. Operator can choose apply strategy (atomic full apply vs staged patch). We should keep a fallback policy: if required layers missing, installer refuses activation and reports helpful diagnostics + artifact list for offline fetch.

Maria L.: UX ask: we should provide an "ops preview" tool that verifies a bundle locally and prints a minimal remediation plan (missing layers, disk reqs, activation time). Less guesswork at customer site.

Jun (infra): agree. also add a small explorer UI that maps layers -> packages and shows dedupe savings estimate. customers will like the storage-savings pitch.

Sasha P.: noted. next steps: 1) prototype a manifest format (v1) + streaming-apply harness, 2) update verifier agent to accept layer-index handshake, 3) wire up offline bundle CLI that emits a locator file and verification summary. I'll spin a spike and link PR.

Kevin T.: sounds good. include concrete failure scenarios in the spike: mid-apply power loss, missing optional layer marked required by mistake, and partial activation rollback.

deploy-bot: CI job #flux/build-packaging-spike started — pipeline: packaging-spike -> artifactize -> unit-tests. <https://ci.internal/redwood/flux/1234>

Maria L.: thanks — ping us when PR exists and we'll take ops/pm review. :party_popper:

Sasha P.: will do. tagging @jun for infra estimates when spike PR lands. :wave:
